chapter_title: [Concer]ning why, if the Person shall look down into Water, [ ... ]
chapter_note: This chapter preserves correspondential teaching that maps physical observations (water reflection, shadows) onto cosmic events and body-cosmos correspondences. The substrate is dominant: inverted reflection maps to the descent of the Summons and ascent of the Obedience, to stellar-zodiacal parentage of earthly beings, to birth inversion, and shadow-earth connection maps to the body's origin from the abyss. No institutional or exhortation content. Editorial material consists entirely of dialogue frame and pedagogical framing phrases ('I reveal to you', 'listen and I may teach you'). Gardner notes 'loosely grouped teachings' that 'may evidence textual development' — consistent with several originally independent correspondential units joined by editorial transitions. The negative editorial fatigue score reflects frame material concentrated at the chapter's opening. The teaching represents what Gardner calls Mani's 'totally integrated science' — natural phenomena explained through cosmic correspondence.

paragraphs.core_text: When the person is above water and looking down [into the wat]ers, if he shall see his face reflected why shall you find his head turned upside down and also his feet upwards? Yet, when he stares down into the waters, his face shall not be visible, nor can he see it there?
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed dialogue frame opening: '[Once again, one of his disciples asked the apostle ...] instruct me about this lesson:' — formulaic attribution wrapping a substantive observational question.
paragraphs.temporal_note: The question defines the teaching structure: two physical observations (inverted reflection; invisibility when looking straight down) that the subsequent paragraphs will map onto cosmic correspondences. The question itself is substantive — it sets up the entire teaching sequence. Persian pedagogical tradition.

Pure dialogue frame: 'Then the apostle says to him:' followed by a general transitional statement ('this universe is established of mystery'). The claim that the universe is full of mystery is a framing assertion that prepares for the teaching — it does not itself map domain onto domain. Very high dialogue_frame score (52.17).

paragraphs.core_text: [And] this: The face of people and the shape of trees shall appear turned upside down in the water as this is signified in [the] mystery of the summons, when it was sent down to the worlds of Darkness towards the First Man. Sin[ce ...] in this way it cast itself down [...] like a person [who] plunges headlong into water; so it is also with the summons. It cast itself headlong to the worlds below, with strength and diligence.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Maps physical observation (inverted reflection) → cosmic event (descent of the Summons/Call to the First Man in the worlds of Darkness). Both sides of the mapping stay within the cosmic system. The Summons plunging headlong corresponds to the inverted image in water. '[And] this:' functions as a teaching-unit marker within the correspondential sequence. Lacunae preserve manuscript damage.

paragraphs.core_text: And this too: Shall the person lift his head up from the water, his face shall not be visible to him, being bent below. This characterises the mystery of the obedience that ascended from below, from with the First Man his father to the Living Spirit.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed closing pedagogical frame: 'This is a spiritual mystery that I have [revea]led to you so that you would understand it.' — first-person revelation claim ('I have revealed') and audience address ('so that you would understand it') are editorial voice.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Maps the second physical observation from paragraph 1 (can't see face when looking up) → cosmic event (ascent of the Obedience/Answer from the First Man to the Living Spirit). Completes the paired cosmic mapping: Summons descends (¶3), Obedience ascends (¶4). Both sides cosmic. 'And this too:' is a teaching-unit connector paralleling '[And] this:' in ¶3. The Summons-and-Answer pair (Call and Obedience) is a fundamental substrate cosmological structure.

paragraphs.core_text: The face of people and of animals and of trees is visible in the water, hanging upside down. This occurs to the mystery of the stars and the zodiac, which hang upside down and are visible in the great sea. For the face of people and beasts and all trees hang on the root of the stars and the zodiac, being begotten from them. Just as their fathers, who are spread out above, hang upside down; so it is also that the mystery of their fathers is being revealed to them whenever they stare down into the water. This is, that you shall find their shapes inverted.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed pedagogical opening: 'If you wish to understand another corporeal mystery on this subject, listen and I may teach you to understand it.' — second-person address ('you'), pedagogical voice ('listen and I may teach you'), editorial transition from the 'spiritual mystery' of ¶4 to the 'corporeal mystery' here.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Maps inverted reflection → stars and zodiac hanging inverted in 'the great sea,' with earthly beings (people, animals, trees) 'begotten from' and 'hanging on the root of' their celestial parents. Classic body-cosmos / zodiac-body correspondence. The concept of stellar 'fathers' whose forms are revealed through water-reflection is deeply correspondential. Both sides of the mapping stay within the cosmic system. The spiritual/corporeal distinction (noted by Gardner as a redactor's organizing principle) is an editorial classification imposed on substrate material.

paragraphs.core_text: Not only this, but [the] child who is born; as the ho[ur] approaches for him to be born, he hangs upside down and is born head first. Indeed, due to this, his mystery shall be revealed in these waters people stare down into.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Maps the physical process of birth (child inverted, born head first) → the inversion mystery visible in water. Body-cosmos correspondence: the birth process itself enacts the cosmic inversion pattern. Both sides within the natural/cosmic system. 'Not only this' is a teaching-unit connector continuing the correspondential sequence. No editorial voice, no institutional content.

paragraphs.core_text: Behold, you will find the shadow of the person who walks along is joined to the earth all the time. If the person is troubled [...] his shadow up upon the earth [...] above. It is impossible for him to do [... ...] on the earth. See, this mystery is [a] great sign, signifying that the entire body came from the earth and had ascended from the abyss. Again, due to this, its shadow is joined on the earth, turned downwards, and hanging from above.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed editorial transition: 'Furthermore, I reveal something else to you:' — bridge connective ('Furthermore') plus first-person pedagogical voice ('I reveal something else to you'). Seam flag correctly detected the bridge connective, though the subsequent content remains cosmic rather than institutional.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Maps shadow permanently joined to earth → body's origin from earth/abyss. Classic body-cosmos correspondence: the shadow's earthward binding reveals the body's material origin. Both sides within the cosmic system. The bridge connective detected by the seam flag marks an editorial TRANSITION between originally separate teaching units (reflection teachings → shadow teaching), but the content itself is substrate. Significant lacunae may obscure additional correspondential detail. Gardner identifies this as the chapter's final teaching unit.
